properties.value: Posture-control candidate list, NOT a confirmed weakness: sampled sites are mostly null-checks and non-adversarial equality on hash-NAMED values (e.g. `if (digest == null)`, `blurHash != null`, backup contentsHash equality in SignalBackupAgent), while the security-critical MAC/digest verifications correctly use MessageDigest.isEqual (tracked as ALG-36a15216). Treat the remaining site list as candidates for review; no security-context non-constant-time comparison was confirmed in the samples read

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CBC (unauthenticated mode, always paired with a separate MAC in this codebase): legacy local storage via MasterCipher (AES/CBC/PKCS5 + HMAC-SHA1, 128-bit MasterSecret key), archived-attachment decryption via AttachmentCipherInputStream.createCipher (line 302, AES-256-CBC key + outer/inner HMAC-SHA256), the lib/archive EncryptedBackupWriter/Reader backup frames, and the internal-settings backup playground. CBC's known risks (no integrity, padding oracles) are mitigated by the MAC-verify-then-

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA1 in two roles: (1) TOTP — the Key URI whitelist maps HmacSHA1/SHA256/SHA512 (TotpRepository.kt:45-49); RFC 6238 TOTP is HMAC-SHA1 by default, and the account's TOTP parameters are server-chosen. (2) LEGACY local crypto — MasterCipher/MasterSecret/AsymmetricMasterCipher authenticate local storage with HMAC-SHA1 (encrypt-then-MAC style), and the PBKDF2-derived key spec at MasterSecretUtil.java:342. HMAC-SHA1's digest is quantum-weakened (Grover); fine for TOTP lifetimes, weak-by-modern-st

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CTR (stream mode, no integrity — MACs applied separately): legacy backup frames (BackupFrameOutputStream/RecordInputStream, AES/CTR/NoPadding with HMAC-SHA256 over frames), glide disk-cache encryption (EncryptedCoder.java:47,86), and local backup metadata. CTR with a proper MAC is sound; nonce management is the classical risk. PQ impact only via Grover margin. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The GOOD posture-control record: MessageDigest.isEqual used for APK update digest verification (ApkUpdateInstaller.kt:84,180), legacy backup MAC verification (BackupRecordInputStream.java:125,168,189), and digest validation — constant-time comparisons of authenticator tags. Kept so the inventory shows where comparisons are done correctly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transport config: explicit cipher-suite allowlists (GMAPS_CONNECTION_SPEC lines 86-105, GMAIL_CONNECTION_SPEC lines 107-121) pinned to TLS 1.2 for Signal's censorship-circumvention reflector traffic to Google hosts (HostConfig at lines 193-195). All permitted KEX is ECDHE_ECDSA/ECDHE_RSA (plus static TLS_RSA_* suites reported separately) — quantum-vulnerable key agreement, harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure. Changeable here only to the extent the reflector servers support TLS 1.3 hybrid groups.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The X25519 identity keypair is Signal's core trust anchor: these prefs keys name where the Curve25519 identity keys (pref_identity_public_curve25519, legacy) and the asymmetric master secret curve25519 keys are stored, and AccountValues.kt:702 migrates them into the encrypted KeyValueStore. The X25519 ECDH itself runs inside the libsignal Rust library (binary dependency, not this repo) — quantum-vulnerable under Shor; migration is the PQXDH hybrid (already partially deployed here via Kyber preke

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA256 — the app's main MAC: legacy backup frame authentication (BackupFrameOutputStream.java:66-71 / BackupRecordInputStream.java:86-87, keys HKDF-split from the backup passphrase KDF), archived-attachment outer/inner MACs (AttachmentCipherInputStream.initMac, verified with MessageDigest.isEqual via MacValidatingInputStream), and TOTP SHA256 support. HMAC-SHA256 keeps adequate PQ margin (Grover reduces key search to 2^128 — still fine). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AEAD workhorse of the app: Signal installs its own native AesGcmProvider as the highest-priority JCA provider (ApplicationContext.java:360 — a homegrown crypto provider, class-6 asset), Android Keystore AES-GCM sealing of database/attachment secrets (KeyStoreHelper.seal), attachment/profile encryption, plus AES-GCM TLS suites in the reflector specs. AES-GCM is Grover-degraded but acceptable post-quantum at 256-bit keys. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 digests for attachment digests (AttachmentUploadUtil, AttachmentTable backfill), incremental MAC chunk hashes validated via DigestValidatingInputStream, group title hashing (GroupTable.kt:189), HKDF inputs, and S3/CDN integrity. Standard hash; quantum impact only via Grover (collision 2^128→2^64 effective on attacker-controlled inputs — no practical break for these uses). Changeable here if needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 appears as TLS cipher suites in the reflector allowlists (TLS_ECDHE_*_AES_128_GCM_SHA256/CBC, TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_*) and in the legacy MasterSecret chain: MasterSecret.java derives an AES-128 encryption key and MasterSecretUtil.java:250-251 generates an AES-128 key (PBEWITHSHA1AND128BITAES-CBC-BC). AES-128 gives only 64-bit Grover margin — 256-bit preferred for long-lived data-at-rest (backups, database). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The deployed post-quantum asset: Kyber-1024 (ML-KEM-1024) last-resort and one-time KEM prekeys, generated in PreKeyUtil.generateKyberPreKey (each public key signed by the Ed25519 identity key at PreKeyUtil.java:192), stored in SignalKyberPreKeyStore, synced by PreKeysSyncJob, and consumed server-side for PQXDH hybrid key agreement. Signal already ships the PQ migration target for its ECDH half — strongest available parameter set. Changeable only by protocol version in libsignal.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 (libsignal HKDF) derives backup frame keys (BackupFrameOutputStream/RecordInputStream "Backup Export"), GV2 group master keys from group IDs (GroupId.kt:316), attachment/backup key material, and demo backup reader keys. KDF itself is PQ-safe given a PQ secret input; its inputs (X25519 shared secrets) are the quantum-vulnerable part. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: LEGACY passphrase lock screen KDF (MasterSecret era): SecretKeyFactory "PBEWITHSHA1AND128BITAES-CBC-BC" with a benchmark-scaled iteration count targeting 50ms — MINIMUM_ITERATION_COUNT = 100 (MasterSecretUtil.java:281), far below OWASP's 310k minimum for HMAC-SHA1-class KDFs. Output keys feed AES-128 + HMAC-SHA1 local encryption. CWE-916-grade weakness, but the MasterSecret path is legacy/deprecated in favor of the keystore-sealed DatabaseSecret; low reachability today.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 drives a HOMEGROWN passphrase KDF: FullBackupBase.getBackupKey iterates MessageDigest SHA-512 250,000 rounds over the passphrase+salt and trims to 32 bytes (FullBackupBase.java:15-31) — a custom construction (not PBKDF2/Argon2) protecting the legacy backup passphrase; iterated enough to be defensible but a copy-paste-style custom KDF worth flagging for review. CallingAssets.kt:148 hashes call assets. SHA-512 retains good PQ margin. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 at the strong end: Aes256Ctr32 (libsignal) encrypts the local backup metadata key (LocalArchiver.kt:242), legacy backup frames use a 32-byte HKDF-split AES-CTR key (BackupFrameOutputStream), and AES_256_GCM/CBC TLS suites appear in the reflector allowlists. 256-bit keys retain comfortable margin against Grover. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS_ECDHE_*_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 suites in the GMAPS reflector allowlist (SignalServiceNetworkAccess.kt:89,92) — modern AE suites paired with quantum-vulnerable ECDHE key exchange over TLS 1.2. The AE itself is PQ-acceptable. Changeable here only with server-side suite support.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The app's randomness source: SecureRandom for prekey IDs, master/backup keys (Util.getSecretBytes), salts, IVs, attachment IDs, and TOTP. Correct CSPRNG choice throughout; the weak-random rule's SecureRandom sites in ALG-7d1fdc12 were rejected as false matches. Non-security kotlin.random usage (job jitter, UI) exists elsewhere and is not a security-context weakness.

properties.value: Two PKI assets: (1) device transfer generates a self-signed X.509 identity from libsignal's DeviceTransferKey and serves TLS with it (SelfSignedIdentity.java:56-67; client side uses an ApprovingTrustManager — TOFU-style user-approved trust); (2) MobileCoin fog-authority trust roots are loaded from committed PEM raw resources via CertificateFactory("X.509") (MobileCoinConfig.java:47-54) — a committed trust store for the payments fog service. Both are real, live X.509 handling. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed keystore in libsignal-service TEST resources (ias.jks — fixture for Intel Attestation Service / SGX-related test paths). Test-only key material; no production key ships here. Recorded as committed key material (class 3/4) with test-fixture scope; the binary was not parseable in-scan, so entries inside the store are unenumerated — noted as a coverage limitation rather than a gap.
